pageCache.pageTitle: Aims and Ethos - London Park Schools
pageCache.text:
London Park Schools offers a fresh approach to secondary schooling, one that is dynamic, forward-thinking, and deliberately designed around a tight-knit school community. By ensuring every child is deeply known, fully supported, and consistently stretched, LPS unlocks new levels of confidence and capability in students, so they can thrive thanks to LPS’ unique, experiential approach to learning, students are equipped not only with strong academic foundations, but also with the skills, self-belief, and adaptability they need to succeed in their future endeavours.
The LPS values: Our four ‘Cs’ of success Our four Cs are at the heart of all that we do. These values empower each student to think independently, engage actively, develop the important problem-solving skills necessary for future success, and learn to lead with integrity.

pageCache.pageTitle: Aims & Ethos | Private School Westminster | LPS Mayfair
pageCache.text:
At LPS Mayfair we believe education is about growing minds, growing character, and growing the values that shape how we treat one another.
Our school ethos, ‘Learn Like a Londoner’ reflects our location at the heart of a global capital and our embrace of the energy, diversity, and opportunity that it brings. It means learning from the world around us, being curious, open-minded, and bold in our thinking.
The LPS values: Our four ‘Cs’ of success
These powerful values are embedded into every part of school life, from how we teach and learn, to how we resolve challenges, build community, and encourage responsibility.
They shape not only who our students are today, but the citizens, creators and leaders they’re becoming.

pageCache.pageTitle: Head's Welcome | Senior School London | LPS Mayfair
pageCache.text:
A very warm welcome to London Park School Mayfair, Sixth & Hybrid.
Here in the heart of Mayfair, overlooking Green Park and Buckingham Palace, our school sits in one of the most remarkable locations in London. The Grade I listed home of the Sixth Earl of Coventry, and private club for the likes of Churchill and Ian Fleming, 106 Piccadilly is a building steeped in history. But what truly defines us is not the grandeur of our surroundings – it is the life, warmth and energy within them.
Just like London itself, our community is wonderfully diverse. British and international students learn side by side, forming friendships that cross cultures and perspectives.
When I am asked what I hope our students leave with, beyond excellent results, my answer is always the same; I want them to develop their unique character, to be curious, discerning and big‑hearted. I want them to understand the power of their own voice and to use it with intention. And I want them to experience the contagious sense of joy that comes from learning in a community that genuinely sees and values them.
You will find that spirit everywhere here. In the conversations that spill out of lessons. In the confidence with which students share their ideas. In the kindness they show one another. In the way they embrace both the intimacy of a small school and the extraordinary opportunities of a world‑class city. I hope you will come and visit our wonderful school and meet our incredible students. We would be delighted to welcome you into our community.
Head, LPS Mayfair, Sixth & Hybrid

pageCache.pageTitle: Sport & PE | Secondary School Mayfair | LPS Mayfair
pageCache.text:
School sport builds healthier, more confident and better engaged students by strengthening wellbeing, resilience, teamwork and academic focus. That’s why we offer a diverse range of sports alongside a strong foundation in physiology, empowering students to manage their wellbeing beyond the classroom.
Our highly sought-after GCSE PE programme reflects this commitment. Throughout the year, students gain a wealth of opportunities to extend their learning, including competitive ISA events, dedicated small schools’ tournaments and exposure to elite training facilities.
Our partnership with LPS Clapham enables us to run bigger games afternoons, with greater resources, stronger teams, more fixtures and specialist coaching. We also continuously expand our sports offerings, incorporating unique options like climbing, golf, boxing, and rowing, as well as offering specialist sport trips and opportunities like our Porto football tour where students play competitive matches against local schools, attend professional training and enjoy attending professional games. This is one of the many ways we get the best of both worlds, capturing the benefits of being a tight-knit school, with big school perks.
The core sports on offer during our games afternoons include Football, Netball, Rugby, Cricket, Hockey, Tennis, Rounders, and Padel. However, we appreciate that competitive sport isn’t for everyone. At LPS Mayfair students can choose a multi-sport option within games where the focus is on enjoyment, participation and teamwork. Students are exposed to a variety of sports every week, with the goal of finding something each student can fall in love with. These options include dodgeball, handball, Gaelic football, capture the flag, table tennis and many more.
Most lessons and fixtures take place at the Spencer Club, one of London’s finest sporting facilities with first-rate playing fields and courts. Through partnerships with specialist facilities our students have access to world-class professional facilities and coaching for specialised sports like cycling, boxing, padel, water sports and more.
We nurture our most talented athletes through the Elite Performance Pathway, a programme that offers strength and conditioning support, university-led fitness testing, and access to resources designed to broaden knowledge of nutrition, leadership, and sports psychology.

Neighboured by the storied West End, it’s no surprise that LPS Mayfair has a rich and flourishing creative arts offering.
Music
We offer group and individual tuition, taught by working musicians, who alongside their work at LPS are performing at the highest level, touring with household name artists or playing in leading orchestras. Students choose from a broad range of instruments, from piano and vocals to drums, trumpet and saxophone, while bands, choirs and regular concerts ensure there are ample opportunities to perform. In addition to instruments, students bring their creativity to composition and music production. LPS Mayfair students are the proud winners and current reigning champions of the Independent Schools Association composer competition three years running. Lessons frequently take students to the best that London has to offer to learn the industry first-hand; professional recording studios, west end theatres and renowned music venues, such as the Royal Albert Hall.
Art
Students explore a range of mediums and techniques in our lofty, light filled art studio. To offer students every opportunity to tap into their creativity, students enjoy internal and external workshops hosted by experts in that craft. To learn from the greats, and foster inspiration and imagination, students venture beyond our doors to the finest galleries and studios – big and small.
Drama
Whole-school productions, seasonal showcases and GCSE and A Level performances mean it’s an exciting calendar of performance at LPS Mayfair. Whether on stage or behind the scenes students are exposed to the range of opportunities in performance and hopefully finding a craft where their creativity can flourish. Major productions take place at The Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, allowing students to work in an industry level setting. Key to our drama offering is group and individual tuition in LAMDA, a world-leading drama school, training and inspiring exceptional artists for over 160 years.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our History | Secondary School Mayfair | LPS Mayfair
pageCache.text:
Follow in the footstep of greats in 106 Piccadilly
The site of London Park Mayfair is steeped in a rich history. The original townhouse over looking Green Park, was built for Sir Hugh Hunlock in 1761. In 1764 – and for the next two centuries – it became ‘Coventry House’, the home of Lord Coventry and his family. Robert Adam, the famous architect carried out important interior updates in 1765 and many of the building’s designs are mirrored in some of the UK’s most iconic buildings. It remained as Coventry House until 1848 when it was briefly home to the French Ambassador.
After some important interior upgrades, it re-emerged as St James’s Club in 1868 and then the Bachelor’s club. Remodelled by Thomas Cundy Senior, it remained as the club until its demise in 1978. During this time, it was frequented by many luminaries of the day, including Evelyn Waugh and Ian Fleming. Some say that it was in 106 that some of today’s most loved novels were first incepted.
The interior is arranged over four storeys with a basement. Internally, most of the 18th century features have been retained. The main entrance hall has a grand stone staircase with a wrought iron balustrade, which splits into two flights at first floor level. On the ground and first floors there are several ornate ceilings with intricate detail, as well as chandeliers, marble pillars and ornate cornicing.
This building is awe-inspiring and provides a constantly stimulating environment for learning, for both students and staff alike. Whilst our environment is old, our outlook and approach is anything but.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pastoral Care | Private School Mayfair | LPS Mayfair
pageCache.text:
Students describe LPS Mayfair as feeling like a family. The tight-knit community that LPS Mayfair fosters is thanks to our award-winning pastoral care, which is the golden thread running through everything we do. At LPS every student is known, and every voice is heard. Key to our family feeling is the vertical tutoring and house system.
Vertical tutoring sees students’ form classes made from students across years 7-11 and a dedicated form tutor. Blending ages in this way enables students to feel greater belonging and connection at school, as well as developing more resilient peer relationships, reducing social silos and year group pressures. Vertical tutoring also allows offers greater continuity of care as tutors work with students for multiple years.
Each form belongs to a House, named after one of our local parks; Green Park, Hyde Park, and St James’s Park. Through the house system students engage in a robust pastoral curriculum, as well as enjoy healthy competition and build camaraderie across a weekly and termly merit competition and inter-house matches, challenges and competitions throughout the year. Sixth formers are part of the House system and take a leadership role, joining in weekly and leading assemblies as well as helping to organise whole school events, offering the benefits of mentoring and leadership across the student body.
A dedicated pastoral lead has overarching responsibility for the students within each House, providing a holistic approach to pastoral care. They oversee students’ wellbeing, monitor academic progress, maintain safeguarding oversight, and promote active participation in the co-curricular programme, ensuring that each student is known, supported, and challenged to thrive both in and beyond the classroom.
All students have access to the on-site counsellor who helps students with specific concerns, as well as equipping students with essential life skills they need to thrive.

Nothing matters more than the safety and wellbeing of our students. The wellbeing of our students isn’t just a priority; it’s a guiding principle. Every child should feel safe, supported, and known. We work hard to build a culture where care, kindness, and trust underpin everything we do. Every student should feel they belong.
Every member of staff at LPS Mayfair is trained in safeguarding and child protection, and we follow clear procedures to ensure that students feel safe, heard and supported.
Our Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) is Hannah Sheehy, Senior Deputy Head, supported by a trained team of deputy DSLs. If you have any concerns about the safety or welfare of a child, your own or anyone else’s, please contact Hannah Sheehy or another member of the safeguarding team immediately.

Together we’re extraordinary
London Park Schools is part of the Dukes Education family of schools and educators, brought together by a common purpose: to give children the foundations for an extraordinary life.
About Dukes Education
Dukes Education is a family of schools, teachers, learners, and parents connected by our pursuit of an extraordinary life for every member of our community.
Our philosophy is to support each individual to live with purpose, to encourage a love of learning, and to act as a team. All of this is underpinned by a quality standard that runs through everything we do.
We believe that education is a journey to be enjoyed and shared at every stage of life, unlocking possibilities for every student.
To learn more about the Dukes Education family, visit dukeseducation.com
We create clusters of nurseries and schools in village locations to ensure that families can enjoy the option of an all-through education journey with Dukes Education within their local area.
Continuity and Confidence
As students move through their educational journey, our guaranteed entry policy offers a seamless progression within the Dukes family, with assured entry at key entry points such as Year 7 and Year 12. This transition is subject only to the availability of a place and a child’s ability to thrive within the school’s ethos and curriculum, providing continuity without the need for traditional entrance exams like the 11+.
Guaranteed Placement, Tailored Support
Dukes Education is committed to supporting each child’s journey into senior school. We work closely with families to ensure each student finds their place, supporting their unique strengths and aspirations.
Our commitment to providing a guaranteed place at a Dukes senior school allows students to focus on their personal and academic growth without the added pressure of entrance exams. For families opting to apply to other selective senior schools, our prep schools offer comprehensive guidance, tailored 11+ preparation, and outstanding pastoral support, ensuring that each student is fully prepared to perform at their best.
For families who decide their child will not sit the 11+ entrance test, we are often able to confirm a place in a Dukes senior school such as LPS Clapham or LPS Mayfair, by September of Year 6. Early acceptance offers peace of mind, allowing students to enjoy their final years of prep school with confidence, focusing on a positive and seamless transition to senior school.
The Dukes Club is an extraordinary community of parents, pupils, staff and alumni that connects families across all the Dukes Education nurseries, schools and colleges. It is a space to learn, network, take advantage of exciting opportunities and amazing rewards, and make new friends. If you are a parent with a child at a Dukes Education school, college or nursery, we warmly invite you to join. As a growing family of education settings, our scale and scope enable us to provide you with exclusive access to a huge array of opportunities that would simply be beyond the reach of any single school.
The Dukes Foundation
The Dukes Foundation was born out of the belief that a person’s early years are their most formative – the ones that shape us into who we’ll be. With our roots in education, we know how vital it is for young people to have the right support, encouragement, and opportunities during this important chapter in their lives.
We want to harness the powerful and uniting spirit of Dukes Education to make a meaningful difference in ways far beyond the boundaries of our organisation. To create a world of inspiration. To see through adversity, to see the potential in every person and to find opportunity in every corner of the world.
Through grant-making and partnerships, we proudly support life-changing charities and organisations who share our ambition. From education and financial assistance, to health, well-being and environmental causes, we can create sparks that can ignite brighter futures.
Find out more about the Dukes Foundation
Dukes Plus is a provider of university application support, life-changing career and university experiences, day camps, tuition, and summer schools.
We are here, so you can get there
By bringing together our exceptional brands under Dukes Plus, we can provide a complete range of industry-leading services that assist students throughout their educational path, nurturing their development and establishing a solid groundwork for a bright future.

pageCache.pageTitle: Clubs & Societies | Best Independent School | LPS Mayfair
pageCache.text:
Running until 5.00pm, after school clubs at LPS Mayfair are driven by student demand. We offer a mind-boggling variety of music, creative, sporting and academic clubs, from Lego robotics to chess to creative writing, to mindfulness to badminton. Our clubs make the most of our central location; Padel at Padel Yard in Vauxhall or Boxing at BuddhaBox in Mayfair, learning from specialist instructors in world-class facilities is a normal day at school for LPS Mayfair students.
We’re confident there is a club for every student to fall in love with – and if there isn’t we can add it to the mix thanks to our demand-based approach to clubs. In addition to specialist clubs, a homework club runs Monday to Thursday for students who prefer to do their homework at school, with the support of a teacher.
Majority of clubs are free, occasionally a club will incur a small charge which will be communicated at the start of term.

pageCache.pageTitle: Curriculum | Senior School Piccadilly | LPS Mayfair
pageCache.text:
Our Learn like a Londoner curriculum is more than a catchy strapline; it captures our entire philosophy of learning. At LPS Mayfair, education is experiential, immersive and practical. Students do not learn about the world from a textbook, they engage with it directly, using London and its extraordinary institutions as an extension of the classroom.
During the school day, teachers make purposeful use of the school’s surroundings to enrich lessons and deepen understanding. The leafy Royal Parks that surround our school, nearby cultural hotspots of the West End, Piccadilly Circus and Covent Garden, as well as world-renowned institutions like the Royal Academy of Arts, the Royal Opera House and the British Museum, are all seamlessly woven into the school day, providing opportunities for students to observe, question, investigate and apply what they have learned in a real-world context. Beyond the immediate neighbourhood, carefully coordinated trips take students further across London and beyond, bringing curriculum content to life and challenging them to think in real world contexts. Museums, theatres, universities, laboratories and professional workplaces allow students to encounter experts, explore new environments and see how their subjects operate in practice.
Proactive and purposeful planning by staff who are trained in experiential, hands-on learning, offer an enriched curriculum across all key stages. Students are encouraged to ask questions, gather evidence, solve problems, reflect on what they have seen and make meaningful links between theory and practice. Learning at LPS is relevant and memorable equipping students to develop independence, confidence, curiosity and the ability to apply their knowledge in unfamiliar settings.
